findings.summary: The server side of d976a8b closely follows the approved CODEX-02-C revision and engineering v1.2 (ADR-E02 server-derived identity, latest-consent FOR UPDATE, context fence, scoped receipts before CAS/quota, initial slot, append-only history with deferred matching check, cascades). Evidence is real: 67/67 app tests, the protected PG/HTTP probe, build, the card checker and an exact-commit native CUA run. Two problems block acceptance. First, the UI drops the pending command and the sticky mutation error whenever one passive status poll fails for any reason. After a lost acknowledgment that can lead to a duplicate sibling, which breaks the "retries do not duplicate child" criterion. Second, the required app-side regression for the newly allowed /loop-preview/setup static-shell route is missing. Real consent, privacy review (G-E03/10-A), retained-data handling and public gates stay closed and were not treated as resolved.

findings.title: One failed passive poll discards the pending command and the save error
findings.problem: When a passive refresh (15s poll, focus, pageshow, visibilitychange) fails for any reason, including a transient 503 or a network error that does not confirm loss of permission, the catch handler calls clear(). That sets pending.current=null, wipes the draft, and replaces the existing sticky 'Save could not be confirmed' error with an access error. After a lost acknowledgment on 'Add another child', the original command UUID is gone. Retry then only refreshes, and when the parent re-enters the child a new command_id is created, which makes a duplicate sibling (the initial slot only protects the first child). This breaks card acceptance 'Setup retries do not duplicate household/child' and the 2026-11-12 instructions: 'Preserve original UUID/copied command until confirmed', 'passive poll cannot clear them or resubmit', 'Real mutation errors remain honest/sticky until explicit Retry', 'Changed context/target version or confirmed permission loss clears/hides stale private intent' (a transient failure is not confirmed loss), and 'no routine poll wipe'.
findings.fix_check: Passive refresh failures must not null pending.current, must not reset the draft, and must not overwrite an existing mutation error. Private intent is cleared only on a confirmed change of context or target version, or a confirmed loss of permission or session. Add a real HTTP/React test: (1) a sibling create whose acknowledgment is lost; (2) the next passive GET is forced to fail; (3) Retry. Check that the original command is resent (the children count rises by exactly one) and that the error stayed visible until the explicit Retry.

findings.title: Missing app regression for the /loop-preview/setup static-shell allowlist
findings.problem: The review-2 clarifications require adding exactly /loop-preview/setup and /loop-preview/setup/ to the assetPath allowlist, with protected tests showing both return 200, cross-site requests still get 403, and a scope query gets 404, and then say 'Add the matching app regression.' The protected probe covers this (child_setup_probe.mjs lines 146-150), but no app test touches /loop-preview/setup. The JSDOM test loads /loop-preview/join and never requests the setup shell. A grep of the app repo finds the route only in source and docs, not in tests. If the widened regex in server/adult-http.mjs changes later, the app's own suite will not catch it.
findings.fix_check: tests/loop-child-setup.test.mjs requests /loop-preview/setup and /loop-preview/setup/ from the real createSyntheticAdultAccessServer with a serve function and asserts 200. It also asserts that Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site returns 403 with 'Request denied.', that /loop-preview/setup?scope=x returns 404 with 'Request unavailable.', and that another path such as /loop-preview/setupx stays unavailable. npm test passes.

findings.title: Native CUA does not include the late-response scenario
findings.problem: The instructions say the eight native scenarios must include 'late response' and that 'DOM tests do not replace CUA.' The CUA record says the delayed old private response after a newer loss of permission, and the lost acknowledgment, were checked only by the automated real HTTP/React test, not natively. This is disclosed and the automated evidence is real, but a gap against the literal criterion remains.
findings.fix_check: Either a native CUA observation where a held or delayed GET /adult/setup resolves after a confirmed permission loss and the UI stays at permission_required with no child cards, or an explicit owner note accepting the automated coverage for this sub-case.

findings.title: REPORT.md and the status file are stale
findings.problem: The report still says 'Exact committed-source native record and independent Claude feature review remain pending', but an exact-commit CUA record for d976a8b now exists. .codex/execution/status/CODEX-02-C.json still says state 'blocked' from the earlier report-only run. The handoff record does not match the evidence actually supplied.
findings.fix_check: The report cites the exact-commit CUA record (reviewed_commit d976a8b, observed_at), states its limitations, lists unresolved items and downstream IDs (03-A), and the status JSON matches the controller's current state.

findings.title: Overflow error code is named differently from the probe's domain code
findings.problem: Overflow and clock failures throw code 'unavailable' (status 503). The instructions list the domain code as 'unexpected503' in one place and 'unavailable503' in another, and the probe's code map uses 'unexpected'. HTTP behaviour is the same, but the domain code name is inconsistent.
findings.fix_check: Use the code name the protected probe and contract document use, or document the alias in CHILD_SETUP_CONTRACT.md.

findings.title: Text links fall below the 44px target
findings.problem: The links at the bottom of the setup screen have min-height 24px. Buttons, inputs and selects meet the 44px control target the instructions ask for.
findings.fix_check: Links in .loop-child have a 44px minimum touch target at 320px width.
